INCORRECT FINGER FLEXION DIRECTION

Issue ID: FMCP-BLENDER-HAND-FLEXION-DIRECTION
Status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — SAMPLED CORRECTION APPLIED; PLAYBACK VALIDATION PENDING
First recorded: October 30, 2026
Affected artifact: Hand_Rig_Animation_Final_20261030_v002.blend
Related milestone: End-to-end procedural skeletal rigging, vertex skinning and keyframe animation

Observed behavior

On the original v002 Action, the user reported that fingers bent backward instead of curling toward the palm. This is the historical behavior that opened the issue. The correction follow-up confirmed the cause and reversed the four-finger local-X keys on v003; the tested finger poses now curl toward the palm. That sampled correction is not a complete visual or playback acceptance, so the issue remains partially resolved rather than closed.

The issue concerns the saved prototype’s local bone axes and animation signs, not whether the mesh has vertex groups. The corrected v003 file has a 22-bone custom hand hierarchy, 21 deform bones, an Armature modifier, weights on all 9,584 vertices, and a corrected Action copied from the original Hand_Demo_Animation. Sampled deformation and weight readback passed; continuous playback and broader visual acceptance remain pending. The correction and remaining gates are recorded in the October 30 follow-up below and in the linked execution report.

Root cause status

Confirmed for the four-finger flexion keys. The existing Action used positive local-X values for the four finger chains. A controlled pose test showed that positive local X bent the index away from the intended palm curl; reversing the same channel direction on the four-finger chains produced the intended curl in the sampled poses. No rest-bone, parenting, weight or mesh edits were required. The thumb uses different local channels and was validated separately. The diagnosis is specific to this Action and skeleton; it does not establish a universal sign convention.

The corrected copy is Hand_Rig_Animation_Final_20261030_v003_AnatomicalCorrection.blend. The historical behavior remains associated with the original v002 Action, which has been restored as the baseline.

Original investigation plan (before the correction follow-up)

  1. Reopen an untouched copy of the exact v002 file and capture a neutral front, back, side and palm view. Record the active Action, frame and object transforms.
  2. Derive and label the palm-facing vector from the actual rest-pose geometry. Do not infer it from global X, Y or Z alone.
  3. For one digit at a time, reset all pose bones to rest and rotate one joint around each candidate local axis in both signs. Record bone matrix, joint location, tip trajectory and target/non-target vertex displacement.
  4. Repeat for proximal, middle and distal joints, then test the complete chain. Separate each joint’s contribution before testing parent-child combinations.
  5. Inspect bone roll and compare local axes across the index, middle, ring, pinky and thumb. Check whether a mirror or coordinate conversion is being applied inconsistently.
  6. Compare the generated animation channel values with the single-joint signs that passed the labeled anatomical view. Change only the identified sign/axis on a new versioned copy.
  7. Review neutral, single-finger curl, thumb opposition, partial curl and opening poses in orthographic views. Examine fingertips, palm contact, wrist stability, neighboring digits, weight pinching and mesh self-contact.
  8. Save a new version, independently reopen it, and replay the corrected Action from start to end. Keep the original v002 and recovery file unchanged.

A numerical dot product toward a guessed palm point is insufficient. The test oracle must use the inspected palm plane and human-visible view labels, and the final visual decision remains a separate gate.

Acceptance criteria

The correction follow-up passed the sampled pose and saved-file checks listed below. Keep this issue partially resolved until every required playback and visual gate passes on a saved and independently reopened file:

  1. Each finger flexes toward the palm.
  2. Each finger extends back toward the neutral pose.
  3. Each joint rotates around an appropriate, documented anatomical axis.
  4. Fingertips follow plausible, continuous motion paths.
  5. Neighboring fingers remain within defined unintended-motion tolerances.
  6. Mesh deformation stays stable across the intended range, with no unacceptable collapse or pinching.
  7. The corrected animation replays consistently from its first frame through its final frame.
  8. The original rest pose remains recoverable, and the saved file returns to it exactly within a documented numeric tolerance.
  9. Front, side, back and palm views pass human visual review.
  10. The corrected evidence is recorded in a replacement milestone or explicit closure report; this historical issue remains preserved.

The original v002 defect is partially resolved on v003. Full anatomical acceptance remains NOT VERIFIED until the remaining playback and multi-view criteria pass.

October 30 correction follow-up

The four-finger local-X flexion keys were reversed on a new versioned Action. Frames 12, 27, 42 and 57 evaluated the index, middle, ring and pinky separately; frame 72 tested the thumb; frames 88 and 100 tested combined/partial curls; frame 108 tested a stronger close pose; frame 78 was open; and frame 120 returned to neutral. Blender evaluated the rigged mesh at these frames. The corrected file reopened independently, and the final weight audit still reported all 9,584 vertices weighted, 21,379 assignments and zero non-normalized vertices. The v002 baseline was restored to its original SHA-256.

The frame-108 pose was inspected in current, right and three-quarter viewport captures without obvious collapse or finger crossing. This does not cover every required orthographic view or all animated frames. The live computer-control pipe was unavailable, so continuous timeline playback from start to end is NOT VERIFIED. Therefore the root cause and sign correction are confirmed, but the issue remains partially resolved pending playback and broader visual acceptance.

See Hand rig anatomical correction: execution and validation for file hashes, the full frame matrix, weight readback and remaining gates.
